title: Octopus: CDP-Backed Multi-Profile Browser Automation
description: Octopus is a CDP-backed browser automation system in which any authorized agent can control one or more isolated Chrome or AdsPower profiles through a broker. Agents discover extensions by nickname, acquire independent expiring sessionBindingRef values, and send typed or policy-gated CDP-backed commands to the intended profile. The current version-two relay is a validated transport baseline; fixed bindings and six tab operations must evolve into the many-agent, many-browser automation contract shown here.

views.title: Install Octopus MCP in Hermes Agent

steps.name: Register every allowed Hermes profile
steps.note: Add Octopus to each selected Hermes profile because every profile owns a separate config.yaml and .env.

steps.name: Provision one principal per profile
steps.note: Give each Hermes profile a distinct non-admin token for discovery, session claims, and browser work without owning a target.

steps.name: Keep browser choice out of installation
steps.note: Do not reserve Profile A, B, C, or D here; every Hermes conversation selects an available extension when it needs one.

steps.name: Add the HTTP MCP
steps.note: Run Hermes mcp add against http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp with header authentication and enter only the dedicated token.

steps.name: Limit the tool surface
steps.note: Expose browser-shaped tools through the mcp-octopus toolset; keep administration tools unavailable to the Hermes principal.

steps.name: Test and reload
steps.note: Run Hermes mcp test, reload MCP, and verify that mcp__octopus__list_extensions appears before any session claim exists.

blocks.text:
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\hermes.exe -p <profile> mcp add octopus --url http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp --auth header
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\hermes.exe -p <profile> mcp test octopus

Hermes stores the token in that profile's .env as MCP_OCTOPUS_API_KEY and writes Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_OCTOPUS_API_KEY} to config.yaml.

items.title: Administrator token exposed to Hermes
items.text: An admin token would give the model pairing, rebinding, renaming, and revocation authority; provision a least-privilege principal instead.

items.title: Browser hard-bound during installation
items.text: Installing the MCP must not reserve or replace Profile A, B, C, or any future extension; browser ownership begins only when a session acquires a claim.

items.title: Wrong Hermes profile configured
items.text: MCP configuration is profile-scoped; adding it to one profile does not make it appear in another profile.

blocks.title: Register Octopus once in every allowed Hermes profile; every session can then discover the tool and choose a browser by nickname.

rows: Nickname, status truth, acquire disposition, and capabilities

Default: tabs, navigation, snapshot, script, and other narrow operations

blocks.text:
mcp__octopus__list_extensions({})
← [{ nickname: 'research', status: 'available', acquireDisposition: 'allow', capabilities: ['tabs', 'snapshot'] },
   { nickname: 'ads-sales', status: 'busy', acquireDisposition: 'deny', reasonCode: 'LEASED' }]

mcp__octopus__connect_extension({ nickname: 'research' })
← { sessionBindingRef: 'sbr_…', nickname: 'research', expiresAt: '…' }

mcp__octopus__browser_open_url({ sessionBindingRef: 'sbr_…', url: 'https://example.com' })

mcp__octopus__disconnect_extension({ sessionBindingRef: 'sbr_…' })

Nickname selects the target only during the atomic connect operation; subsequent commands use the session binding so nickname changes cannot reroute live work.

items.title: Debugger permission changes the trust level
items.text: Chrome requires the non-optional debugger permission and warns that the extension can access the page debugger backend and read or change data on all websites.

items.title: DevTools detaches the automation
items.text: Opening Chrome DevTools on an attached tab can trigger chrome.debugger.onDetach; surface a deterministic DEBUGGER_DETACHED result and never silently continue.

items.title: Unbounded CDP events overload the relay
items.text: Network and tracing domains can produce high-volume data; require subscriptions, byte limits, redaction, backpressure, and drop accounting.

items.title: Current minimum Chrome version is too low for debugger keepalive
items.text: Active debugger sessions keep Manifest V3 workers alive from Chrome 118; raise the current minimum from 116 or implement explicit reattach recovery.

blocks.text:
Critical commit rule:
read snapshot → evaluate broker opinion → begin transaction → recheck statusVersion and lease → persist command → deliver after commit
If the version changed, discard the opinion and reevaluate.

blocks.text:
Trace required for every successful command:
MCP_ACCEPT(bindingRef) → BINDING_VALIDATED(principal,target) → POLICY_DECISION → COMMAND_COMMIT → WS_SEND → EXT_ACK → EXT_RESULT → MCP_OBSERVED
Dispatch returns a durable receipt; MCP_OBSERVED is the later terminal-result query. Join by runId + bindingRef + requestId + commandId and verify the resolved target against the profile fixture marker.

steps.name: Generate key

steps.name: Pair
steps.note: A short displayed code confirms the intended local device.

steps.name: Name

steps.name: List availability
steps.note: Expose each unique nickname and factual status to authenticated agents without assigning ownership.

steps.name: Issue sessionBindingRef

steps.name: Prove
steps.note: Reconnects sign fresh challenges instead of reusing the code.

views.title: Dynamic Agent-Session / Extension Binding

steps.name: Pair and nickname extension once
steps.note: The extension authenticates to the broker and receives a unique nickname; pairing registers a target but grants no agent permanent ownership.

steps.name: Authenticate Hermes once
steps.note: The MCP bearer credential resolves to a stable broker principal independent of any particular Hermes conversation or browser.

steps.name: Discover inside the agent session
steps.note: The active Hermes session lists nicknames and broker-owned availability facts when browser work begins.

steps.name: Acquire ephemeral binding
steps.note: The broker atomically reserves the chosen available target and returns sessionBindingRef with expiresAt.

steps.name: Route session calls
steps.note: Every target-specific call carries sessionBindingRef; the broker validates principal, session, and TTL before routing.

steps.name: Release or expire
steps.note: Explicit release, session close, missed heartbeat, or TTL expiry makes the extension available to another session.

rows: Broker knows the Hermes principal only
Target returns to the available pool
One authoritative lease controls contention and recovery
An MCP transport is not assumed to equal one conversation
Private target ID behind a nickname
Agents never receive raw profile or socket IDs
One active session claim per target by default
A second session waits, gets busy, or chooses another extension
Keep the claim until release or TTL according to policy
Status remains factual while recovery policy controls lease expiry
Abandoned Hermes sessions cannot hold browsers forever

items.title: Raw extension ID used as sessionBindingRef
items.text: This exposes broker identity and lets callers couple to browser internals; issue a separate opaque capability.

items.title: MCP connection confused with agent session
items.text: A transport can reconnect or be reused, so the broker-issued sessionBindingRef and lease state must be explicit.

items.title: No expiry path
items.text: Require TTL, renew, idempotent release, and cleanup after disconnect or missed heartbeat.

blocks.title: The durable installation identifies Hermes; the ephemeral sessionBindingRef temporarily connects one Hermes session to one selected extension.

views.title: Per-Call Routing Envelope

steps.name: Connect before browser work
steps.note: The agent session sends a nickname and receives sessionBindingRef with a finite expiry.

steps.name: Build browser call
steps.note: The agent attaches sessionBindingRef, a fresh requestId, operation, parameters, deadline, and idempotency key.

steps.name: Authenticate and validate lease
steps.note: The broker derives principal_id from the credential and requires an ACTIVE, unexpired row matching principal and sessionBindingRef.

steps.name: Resolve target
steps.note: Only the broker translates the session claim to its private target_id and current extension connection.

steps.name: Execute and correlate
steps.note: The outcome returns to the originating request while the claim remains available for later calls in the same agent session.

rows: Select and validate one live agent-session claim
Authenticate who is making the call
Prevent duplicate side effects during retry
Keep routing stable during one agent session

blocks.text:
MCP browser call
{ sessionBindingRef, requestId, operation, parameters, deadlineMs, idempotencyKey }

Broker lookup
SELECT target_id FROM browser_session_bindings
WHERE session_binding_ref = :sessionBindingRef
  AND principal_id = :authenticatedPrincipal
  AND state = 'ACTIVE'
  AND expires_at > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;

items.title: sessionBindingRef trusted without authentication
items.text: Anyone who copies the reference could route commands. Always require the matching authenticated principal and active lease.

items.title: Socket ID used as the reference
items.text: Socket identifiers change on reconnect and make a durable binding unreliable.

items.title: Parent process ID used as the reference
items.text: Process and task identifiers are unstable and are not authorization boundaries.

views.title: Many Agents Sharing One Extension

steps.name: Classify
steps.note: Mark the operation shared-read or exclusive-write.

steps.name: Accepted
steps.note: Validate schema, authenticated binding ownership, session, deadline, and operation class.

steps.name: Queued
steps.note: Persist principal, bindingRef, resolved target, requestId, and intent before a socket can receive the command.

steps.note: Send through the currently authenticated target socket.

steps.name: Acknowledged
steps.note: Record receipt separately from browser action completion.

steps.name: Correlate

views.title: One Extension Node per Chrome Profile

steps.name: Wake
steps.note: The extension worker loads identity from extension storage.

steps.name: Connect
steps.note: Open a Native Messaging port; the per-profile companion opens the loopback WebSocket to the gateway.

steps.name: Authenticate
steps.note: Sign the fresh gateway challenge with the paired key.

steps.name: Receive
steps.note: Accept versioned commands for this profile only.

steps.name: Execute
steps.note: Use Chrome APIs or page automation in the local profile.

steps.name: Report
steps.note: Return ACK, progress, result, and checkpoint metadata.

steps.name: Reconnect
steps.note: After suspension, repeat authentication and reconcile state.

blocks.text:
HELLO → CHALLENGE → AUTH → READY
COMMAND → ACK → RUNNING → RESULT
HEARTBEAT refreshes liveness; reconnect replaces the old socket binding.

items.title: Worker suspension

items.text: Never let a connection ID alone reclaim a paired target.
